rules.statement: In GitHub Actions workflows, every `actions/checkout` step sets `persist-credentials: false`, unless the job pushes with the job token.
rules.why: Otherwise the job token is written to `.git/config`, where build, test and third-party code can read it.
rules.check: Look for checkout steps in workflow files that lack `persist-credentials: false` in jobs that never push commits or tags.

rules.statement: Give gate (build/test) jobs only `contents: read`. Run any step that needs `id-token: write` or another write permission, such as a coverage upload, in a separate job, never inside the gate job.
rules.why: Keeping an OIDC-minting permission or a token out of the gate job means third-party build and test code can't reach it.
rules.check: Look for gate jobs that grant `id-token: write` or other write permissions, or that run coverage or test-result upload steps inline.

rules.statement: Authenticate coverage-service uploads (such as Codecov) over OIDC, with the action pinned to a commit SHA, and don't store a long-lived upload token as a secret.
rules.why: A stored token is a long-lived secret that can leak. OIDC with a SHA-pinned action needs no secret and can't be swapped out from under the workflow.
rules.check: Look for Codecov or similar upload steps that use a `token:` secret, that don't set `use_oidc`, or whose action is referenced by tag instead of by full commit SHA.

rules.statement: Keep coverage-service checks informational and never let a coverage upload failure fail the CI run. The gate's own exit code stays the only required verdict.
rules.why: Codecov reports and never gates, so the required check stays the Definition of Done gate. Dependabot or fork runs without an OIDC token must not fail.
rules.check: Look for Codecov project or patch statuses that aren't `informational`, `fail_ci_if_error: true` on upload steps, or a coverage threshold added to the Codecov config.

rules.statement: Exclude generated code from coverage once, at collection in the coverlet runsettings (`obj/`, `Migrations/`, `[GeneratedCode]`). Don't add separate ReportGenerator filters or Codecov `ignore` lists for it.
rules.why: Two filter lists in two syntaxes drift apart. Excluding at collection gives every presenter the same input, so the figures agree.
rules.check: Look for new `ignore` entries in codecov.yml, or assembly/file filters passed to ReportGenerator, that duplicate or diverge from the runsettings exclusions.

rules.why: The compiler puts that attribute on async state machines, lambdas and iterators, so excluding it drops hand-written method bodies from the figure.
rules.check: Look for `CompilerGenerated` or `CompilerGeneratedAttribute` in coverlet `ExcludeByAttribute` settings.

rules.statement: In production code, keep hand-written code out of `Migrations/` folders. Only scaffolded EF Core migrations belong there.
rules.why: Coverage excludes `Migrations/` as generated code, so hand-written code placed there silently drops out of the coverage figure.
rules.check: Look for new non-scaffolded classes (helpers, extensions, configuration) added under a `Migrations/` directory.

rules.statement: Don't exclude shipped hand-written projects, such as hosts, from the coverage figure to raise the number.
rules.why: Shipped code is in scope, so leaving it out hides a gap that matters.
rules.check: Look for assembly or project exclusions in coverage settings that target shipped, hand-written projects.

rules.statement: Make CI test-result and coverage reporting steps presentation-only: they never change the verdict, which stays the test runner's exit code.
rules.why: The reporter only presents results. The gate decides pass or fail.
rules.check: Look for reporting scripts or steps that exit nonzero based on parsed results, or that swallow the runner's exit code.

rules.statement: Have each CI or gate run write test results and coverage into a freshly cleared directory, not into per-run accumulating folders merged by glob.
rules.why: Merging `**/coverage.cobertura.xml` across accumulated `TestResults/<guid>/` folders blends every past run into one misleading figure.
rules.check: Look for report-merging globs over `TestResults/**`, or output directories that the script doesn't clear before the run.
